Wait reverse polarity protection with a diode across the input (cathode to +12V, anode to GND) is a crowbar? Actually a reverse-polarity protection diode is usually placed in series with the positive supply, anode to input, cathode to load, so it blocks reverse current. A diode across the supply (cathode to +, anode to GND) is a reverse-biased clamp that conducts only if the rail is pulled negative. It does not protect against reverse polarity of the input; if the barrel jack is reversed, the +12V net becomes negative relative to GND, D7 conducts and shorts the negative input to GND, likely blowing fuse. The spec says "reverse-polarity/negative-transient protection diode on the 12 V input". It is across, not series. It would only conduct if the rail is pulled negative. If the barrel jack is reversed, the center pin (pin1) becomes negative, so +12V net negative, D7 conducts. Yes. But without fuse, it will short. The spec notes commit title TVS but generic diode. Not anomaly.

Look at spec: "The board is a single ESP32-C3 based controller (U1, ESP32-C3-MINI-1) for a resistive-heating composite-curing oven. It:
- Reads up to 3 K-type thermocouples (U2, U3, U4 — MAX31855KASA, one per thermocouples.kicad_sch zone) over a shared SPI bus (SCK/SO + 3 independent chip-selects CS0–CS2), confirmed by firmware (NUM_THERMOCOUPLES = 3, SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7).
- Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1, using simple bang-bang control (firmware: if average_temp < config.temperature { heater_output.set_high() } else { heater_output.set_low() }).
- Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs, and raises a run fault if a fan stalls.
- Accepts power from either a 12 V barrel jack (J11, run supply) or USB-C 5 V (J12, logic/programming supply), arbitrated by an autoswitching power mux (U5, TPS2121RUXR) and stepped down to 3.3 V logic by a buck converter (U8, AP63203WU).
- Exposes status over Wi-Fi via a small webserver and a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1)."

Wait reverse polarity protection with a diode across the input (cathode to +12V, anode to GND) is a crowbar? Actually a reverse-polarity protection diode is usually placed in series with the positive supply, anode to input, cathode to load, so it blocks reverse current. A diode across the supply (cathode to +, anode to GND) is a reverse-biased clamp that conducts only if the rail is pulled negative. It does not protect against reverse polarity of the input; if the barrel jack is reversed, the +12V net becomes negative relative to GND, D7 conducts and shorts the negative input to GND, likely blowing fuse. Look at spec: "The board is a single ESP32-C3 based controller (U1, ESP32-C3-MINI-1) for a resistive-heating composite-curing oven. It:
- Reads up to 3 K-type thermocouples (U2, U3, U4 — MAX31855KASA, one per thermocouples.kicad_sch zone) over a shared SPI bus (SCK/SO + 3 independent chip-selects CS0–CS2), confirmed by firmware (NUM_THERMOCOUPLES = 3, SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7).
- Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1, using simple bang-bang control (firmware: if average_temp < config.temperature { heater_output.set_high() } else { heater_output.set_low() }).
- Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs, and raises a run fault if a fan stalls.
- Accepts power from either a 12 V barrel jack (J11, run supply) or USB-C 5 V (J12, logic/programming supply), arbitrated by an autoswitching power mux (U5, TPS2121RUXR) and stepped down to 3.3 V logic by a buck converter (U8, AP63203WU).
- Exposes status over Wi-Fi via a small webserver and a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1)."

Let's consider if the netlist has a missing connection for D7: It is on +12V and GND. If D7 is reverse polarity protection, it should be in series with +12V, not across? Wait reverse polarity protection with a diode across the input (cathode to +12V, anode to GND) is a crowbar? Actually a reverse-polarity protection diode is usually placed in series with the positive supply, anode to input, cathode to load, so it blocks reverse current. A diode across the supply (cathode to +, anode to GND) is a reverse-biased clamp that conducts only if the rail is pulled negative. It does not protect against reverse polarity of the input; if the barrel jack is reversed, the +12V net becomes negative relative to GND, D7 conducts and shorts the negative input to GND, likely blowing fuse. The spec says "reverse-polarity/negative-transient protection diode on the 12 V input". It is across, not series. It would only conduct if the rail is pulled negative. If the barrel jack is reversed, the center pin (pin1) becomes negative, so +12V net negative, D7 conducts. Yes. But without fuse, it will short. The spec notes commit title TVS but generic diode. Not anomaly.
